ontology.purpose: Build a process ontology of Intelligence Preparation of the Battlefield (IPB) from ATP 2-01.3 so that an intelligence-support or planning-automation system can answer, for each IPB step and substep, what it is, what its inputs and outputs (products) are, who is responsible, which techniques and tools are used, and how it feeds the military decision-making process. The ontology must also capture the analytic constructs IPB produces (area of operations/interest, terrain and weather effects, threat characteristics, threat models, courses of action, event templates) as first-class concepts with their defining properties.
ontology.scope: IN SCOPE: IPB fundamentals, purpose, and staff relationships; IPB support to planning and decision making (MDMP, targeting, information collection); the four IPB steps and their substeps — define the operational environment, describe environmental effects on operations (terrain via OAKOC, weather, civil considerations via ASCOPE/PMESII-PT), evaluate the threat (threat characteristics, threat models, high-value targets), determine threat courses of action (situation templates, event templates and matrices, decision support); IPB products and their components; considerations for unified action and unique environments (urban, subterranean, cyberspace, etc.); checklists, tools, and threat-characteristic categories for regular, irregular, and hybrid threats given in the appendices. OUT OF SCOPE: specific threat-nation order of battle, collection-asset technical data, and joint-level JIPOE procedures beyond what this document restates.
